Sentence (English): I recently got to try out the dishwasher, which is called "3rd Generation Auntie."
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher Auntie is the best ] || ---------------- || I recently got to try out the dishwasher, which is called "3rd Generation Auntie." I was so excited! I'll leave a detailed review. There are two types of dishwashers, and the one I tried was the built-in one. I went to Hae-O Mart to try it out before buying, and they said the built-in one was available for my apartment, which was perfect. Installation process (date changeable): First, after purchasing, I received a KakaoTalk message from Samsung Electronics via Happy Call. I requested a date change, and they were able to adjust it immediately, allowing me to proceed with the renovation preparatory work on my desired date. The technician came and remodeled the space to store the dishwasher. The length was exactly 1cm off, so he cut it a little more to fit perfectly and remodeled it neatly. The technician was also very friendly and helpful. A day or two after the renovation, a separate technician came again to install the dishwasher. I had to change the date at short notice, but he was able to adjust it again and make it fit perfectly. Design and appearance: I was worried the Glam White product might be too white, but the glossy ivory made it even prettier. It's a built-in product, so it fits perfectly under the sink. It looks really neat. Kitchens can look messy even with the slightest mess. It's nice that it's built-in, so it's clean and spacious. The washing mode. The dishes are a daily chore, and they add up with every meal, so it's really convenient to have someone else do it for you. There are several modes, but on automatic mode, it takes about 2 to 2.5 hours. The order is pre-wash, main wash, rinse, hot water rinse, dry, and then finish. The standard mode is best for medium loads and takes about 55 minutes. There's almost no vibration or noise, so it's very quiet. The door opens automatically after washing. It's humid these days, so it took about 2 to 3 hours. When I left the door open, the dishes were completely dry. I think it varies depending on the season. Detergent. There's a detergent dispenser similar to a washing machine, and you can add both detergent and rinse aid. You need to use a special detergent. There are liquid and solid detergents, but I like the liquid tube detergent the best. The technician said that rinse aid isn't often used due to environmental pollution. I actually used only detergent without rinse aid, and it cleaned well and was fine. The interior is divided into three sections. The top section is for small plates, knives, spatulas, ladles, and other utensils. The middle section is for commonly used utensils and cups, and the bottom section is for pots, frying pans, bowls, and spoons. There's a separate spoon compartment inside, but it keeps tipping over when you put it in. This is a bit inconvenient. Cleaning power and capacity. For utensils, you need to play Tetris correctly to ensure the water stream flows through the gaps and cleans thoroughly. Therefore, it's best to place utensils upright, and for rice bowls and pots, turn them upside down for better cleaning. Pots and earthenware pots used for stews like kimchi stew can't be completely cleaned, as any stuck-on seasonings can build up. Therefore, you'll need to rinse them after discarding the food waste. This will help keep the inside of the dishwasher cleaner. It seats 12 people, making it plenty large for a family of four. Overall: Freeing yourself from the hassle of washing dishes is incredibly convenient! I'm so satisfied. I love the color, and since it's built-in, it's clean and nice. No worries this holiday season! It's built-in, so it's clean. The glam white color is perfect. It's spacious for 12 people. Excellent cleaning power. It automatically opens when the cleaning is complete. It's quiet and doesn't vibrate. This review was written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (Original): [ 식기세척기 이모님 최고 ] || ---------------- || 요즘 3대 이모님이라고 하는 식기세척기를 체험해보게 되어서너무 신났어요~! 자세한 후기 남겨보겠습니다.식기세척기는 2가지 타입이 있던데 체험제품은 빌트인이었습니다.체험 전 구매하려고 하0마트에도 가보고 했는데 제가 사는 아파트는 빌트인으로 설치가 가능하다고 해서  딱 맞았어요.✔️ 설치순서(날짜 변경 가능)우선 구매하면 해피콜로 삼성전자에서 카톡이 왔어요.날짜 변경이 필요해서 요청했더니 바로 조정이 가능해서 원하는 날짜에리폼 예비 공사를 진행할 수 있었습니다. 기사님이 오셔서 식세기를 넣을 공간을 리폼하셨는데, 길이가 딱 1cm 정도차이가 나서 크기에 딱 맞게 조금 더 자르고 깔끔하게 리폼해주셨어요.기사님도 매우 친절하시고 좋았어요.리폼 공사 후 1~2일 뒤에 식세기 설치하러 따로 기사님이 다시 오셨는데급하게 날짜를 바꿔야 했는데 또 잘 바꿔서 맞춰주셨습니다.✔️ 디자인 및 외관글램화이트 제품이라 너무 하얀색이 아닐까 했는데광택이 도는 아이보리 느낌이라 더 예뻤어요.빌트인 제품이라 싱크대 하부장에 딱 맞게 들어가서되게 깔끔해 보입니다. 주방은 조금만 어질러져도 지저분해 보이는데빌트인이라 깔끔하고 좋아요~ 집도 넓어보이구요.✔️ 세척 모드설거지 거리는 정말 매일 나오고 매끼니 마다 늘어나는데, 누군가 대신해준다니 정말 편리해요.여러가지 모드가 있는데 자동모드로 돌리면 2시간~2시간 30분 정도 소요가 됩니다.애벌세척 - 본세척 - 헹굼 - 온수헹굼 - 건조 - 완료 순서입니다.표준모드는 양이 보통일 때 사용하는 편이고 55분 정도 걸려요.진동도 거의 없고, 소음도 거의 없어서 매우 조용한 편입니다.세척 후 자동으로 문이 열려요. 요즘은 습해서 2~3시간 쯤문을 열어두니 식기가 다 말랐어요. 계절별로 좀 다를 것 같아요. ✔️ 세제세제는 세탁기처럼 넣는 부분이 생겼고 세제와 린스 2가지를 넣을 수 있습니다.세제는 전용 세제를 사용해야 하구요. 액체와 고체가 있는데액체 튜브형 세제가 가장 좋았아요.기사님 말로는 린스는 환경오염 때문에 잘 사용하지 않는 편이라 합니다.실제로 린스 없이 세제만 사용했는데 세척도 잘되고 괜찮았어요.✔️ 내부 내부는 3단으로 구성되어 있습니다.가장 상단은 작은 접시류와 칼, 주걱, 국자 등 도구를 넣으면 됩니다.중간은 보통 많이 사용하는 식기류와 컵,가장 하단은 냄비나 후라이팬, 대접, 수저 등을 넣으면 좋아요.안쪽에 수저를 넣을 수 있는 수저통이 따로 있는데,수저를 넣으면 자꾸 넘어져요. 이 부분은 좀 불편합니다.✔️ 세척력 및 용량식기류는 테트리스를 잘 해야 물줄기가 사이로 들어가서세척이 깨끗하게 됩니다. 그래서 되도록 식기류는 세워서 넣고,밥공기나 냄비 종류는 뒤집어 놓는 것이 세척이 잘 됩니다.김치찌개 등 찌개류에 사용한 냄비나 뚝배기는 눌러붙은 양념이완전히 깨끗하게 씻기지는 않아서 음식물을 버린 뒤 한번 행궈서 넣어주는 단계가 필요합니다.이렇게 쓴다면 식세기 내부를 좀 더 깨끗하게 유지할 수 있어요~12인용이라 4인 가족이 사용하기에는 아주 충분한 용량입니다.✔️ 총평설거지에서 해방되니 이렇게 편할 수가 없어요!!!!너무 만족스러워요. 색상도 마음에 들고 빌트인이라깔끔하고 좋습니다. 이번 명절에도 걱정 없네요!✔️ 빌트인이라 깔끔✔️ 글램화이트 색상 무난함✔️ 12인용이라 넉넉함✔️ 세척력 우수함✔️ 세척 완료시 자동 오픈✔️ 진동과 소음이 적음 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

This will help keep the inside of the dishwasher cleaner. It seats 12 people, making it plenty large for a family of four. Overall: Freeing yourself from the hassle of washing dishes is incredibly convenient! I'm so satisfied. I love the color, and since it's built-in, it's clean and nice. No worries this holiday season! This will help keep the inside of the dishwasher cleaner. It seats 12 people, making it plenty large for a family of four. It's humid these days, so it took about 2 to 3 hours. When I left the door open, the dishes were completely dry. I think it varies depending on the season. Detergent. This will help keep the inside of the dishwasher cleaner. It seats 12 people, making it plenty large for a family of four. Overall: Freeing yourself from the hassle of washing dishes is incredibly convenient! I'm so satisfied. I love the color, and since it's built-in, it's clean and nice. No worries this holiday season! Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.
