Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

Comments (English): [ It's so nice to have someone do the dishes for me. ] || ---------------- || Why I need it. Even though I'm a family of two, I love cooking. And I love the dishes that come with cooking. It's hard to wash all the dishes at once after eating, so I'm the type who constantly washes dishes while cooking. Now, I don't have to worry about the dishes piling up. The dishwasher will do it for me. Be sure to check this before purchasing! I just found out there are two types of dishwashers. 1. Built-in. As the name suggests, you have to remove the sink cabinet to install it. If the dishwasher and the cabinet don't fit, you'll need to cut out the mop holder. Or, if the dishwasher doesn't fit perfectly, additional work will be required. 2. Freestanding. You can install it separately, rather than built in. (Freestanding is also available as a built-in option. Some people do it themselves, while others pay a professional to do it for a fee.) I had no prior knowledge of the dishwasher, so I thought, "Oh, great opportunity for a dishwasher!" and thought it would install itself. But I ended up getting a big headache. Dishwasher installation process. 1. After purchase, most people come the next day to check the installation environment. The renovation technician will contact you first, make an appointment, and come in person to conduct an inspection. 2. During the inspection, there's no additional installation fee for simple installations, such as cutting out the mop holder. However, if the door inner cabinet or lower cabinet is cut out to secure space, or if the sink cabinet is not removable, the installation will cost between 90,000 and 130,000 won. (We're renting, and the dishwasher didn't fit the lower cabinet at all. We had a separate dishwasher cabinet made, which cost 180,000 won. We connected it to the microwave oven next to it. We also drilled two holes the size of a wall-mounted TV and secured them in place. I wondered why they went to such lengths, but they said it was unavoidable for stability reasons, as the dishwasher might tip forward when the door is opened.) The dishwasher cabinet installation took about two business days. 3. The renovation technician who performed the dishwasher pre-inspection and completed installation preparations, and the Samsung dishwasher installation technician came the next morning and installed the dishwasher in less than 30 minutes. Noise. I recorded the sound on video. Other than the sound of the water sloshing around, it didn't feel loud. I ran it late at night and it worked perfectly. Detergent! Do I really need rinse? There are separate places for dishwasher detergent and rinse. Rinse helps speed up the drying time of dishes and makes them shine. They said that if you use the all-in-one dishwasher, you don't need to use rinse separately! Let's test it out. The default setting is Normal + Intensive Dry, which takes about 1 hour and 50 minutes. (The Intensive Dry button automatically releases when you use rinse.) I thought it was too long. 1. I tried the 59-minute cycle on the Standard setting only. -> The rice bowls, plates, tongs, spoons, chopsticks, scissors, etc. were all cleaned well. I had porridge in a stainless steel pot, so it was quite pressed down, and it didn't clean well. It also barely dried. 2. The default setting of Normal + Intensive Dry. -> All the dishes were cleaned cleanly. Except for the dents in the rice and soup bowls, they were completely dry. The glass bowl for steamed eggs was only half-cleaned, as if the water hadn't reached one side. Using the all-in-one detergent and powerful drying, it definitely dried better than when I used the standard setting. It really washes! People who buy dishwashers often say you have to play Tetris well. I understand why. I've been using it every day for five days now, and I stack the dishes so the water can flow through them properly. It really washes them. If you press the powerful button instead of the standard setting, it even does a preliminary wash. But since food scraps and other debris splash into the dishwasher, it can be difficult to clean. So I set it to the standard setting, and even if it's not a preliminary wash, I just throw away the food and rinse the dishes before putting them back in. The walls are clean, and the mesh basket is clean, so I don't have to worry about it. I'm very satisfied. I rinse the used dishes once with water and stack them neatly. While I'm doing something else, the dishes are done! It's for 12 people. I used it to cook a rice cooker, a pan, a frying pan, a small pot, two plates, two rice bowls, two soup bowls, a strainer, and a porridge bowl all at once. It all fits! Overall review: The design is clean and pretty. It's smaller than I thought, so I wondered if it could serve 12 people, but it really does require a lot of washing. If you're good at Tetris, you'll be able to clean 99% of the dishes. However, if you press down hard enough on a stainless steel pot, it's not very clean.

It's cleaner than my own dishes. It gets rid of rice grime, chili powder, grease, water cup stains, and more. The dishwasher cleans better than I or my husband. I no longer ask, "Why did you do the dishes like this? Can't you make it a little neater?" because they weren't done properly afterward. 2. The kitchen is tidy. My husband and I don't like things hanging out in the dishwasher, but since the dishes are drying inside, there's nothing left on the counter, so the kitchen looks neat. 3. I can do other things while the dishwasher is running. I have a standing job, so I have to stand for 30 minutes to wash the dishes. It's convenient because the dishwasher does that for me. I used to leave the water running and the hot water running when rinsing, but that hasn't happened since I bought the dishwasher. Cons. 1. The dishwasher runs for a long time. Sentence (English): Because the pros far outweigh the cons!
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher. Awesome. ] || ---------------- || My previous house was a lease, so I couldn't install a dishwasher. But this time, I'm moving into my own apartment, so I finally got the dishwasher I've always wanted. Coupang had a big sale, so I got it for a much cheaper price. ^------^. There were more cons than I expected, which was surprising! Still, if someone were to ask me whether I should buy a dishwasher, I'd say yes, definitely buy it! Because the pros far outweigh the cons! I guess I just don't like doing dishes. The biggest pro is that I don't wash them! The biggest con is that the dishwasher spins for a long time! *How I overcame the cons: Just spin the top on high speed. It's done in 30 minutes. I don't use the hot air dryer, leave the door open function on, let it air dry, and clean up the next day. Here's my thoughts on the pros and cons of dishwashers. Pros: 1. It's cleaner than my own dishes. It gets rid of rice grime, chili powder, grease, water cup stains, and more. The dishwasher cleans better than I or my husband. I no longer ask, "Why did you do the dishes like this? Can't you make it a little neater?" because they weren't done properly afterward. 2. The kitchen is tidy. My husband and I don't like things hanging out in the dishwasher, but since the dishes are drying inside, there's nothing left on the counter, so the kitchen looks neat. 3. I can do other things while the dishwasher is running. I have a standing job, so I have to stand for 30 minutes to wash the dishes. It's convenient because the dishwasher does that for me. My husband and I can watch TV during that time. 4. I use less water. I can remove grease or stuck-on food. I used to leave the water running and the hot water running when rinsing, but that hasn't happened since I bought the dishwasher. Cons. 1. The dishwasher runs for a long time. I solved this problem by running it on high speed. 2. Pre-washing. -> My husband says he'll do the dishes instead of pre-washing. Doesn't everyone rinse and soak the food before washing? It's convenient because you can soak them in water and run them all at once in the evening. This might be a drawback for those who find it cumbersome. 3. It requires a lot of dishes. -> We're a two-person household, so the amount of dishes doesn't matter, but families with three or more people will likely need a lot of dishes to run the dishwasher once a day. 4. Salt is expensive. I'm using it without salt because it runs without it. I asked the technician, and he said it doesn't really matter. I'm using it without salt. 5. Some people say the detergent residue makes it look white, but I split the solid detergent in half and use only half, and it works great! I've never had any detergent residue come out.
